data.source: yfinance daily OHLCV via trade-data-equities EquitiesDataClient + YFinanceProvider, adjusted=True (split/div adjusted)
data.range_note: client uses [start, end); end=2026-09-26 includes all 2026-09-25 bars, matching the pre-registered '2010-01-01 through 2026-09-25'

mechanical_choices: M1: walk-forward on daily bars: TRAIN=1260/TEST=252/STEP=252/EMBARGO=21 (21 trading days = 1 month)
M2: month-end = last trading day of calendar month in the union ETF calendar
M3: vol = sample-stdev of the 60 daily returns ending at bar t-1 (excludes the rebalance day's own return) x sqrt(252)
M4: TR needs 252 prior bars (index i >= 252), else leg flat
M5: ETF missing a bar on a rebalance date -> leg flat that month
M7: benchmark = EW 6-ETF B&H, monthly rebalance to 1/6, 5 bps/side on turnover incl. initial allocation, costs at rebalance close; returns subset to OOS timestamps
M8: borrow sensitivity (0/100 bps) is extra runs, report-only; gated run uses the spec 30 bps

gates.name: deflated_sharpe
gates.description: DSR >= 0.95: under the null of no skill, the chance the true Sharpe is positive is at least 95% after correcting for the number of trials.

gates.name: oos_sharpe
gates.description: Median walk-forward out-of-sample Sharpe > 1.0: the edge must survive unseen data, not just the fitted window.

gates.name: max_drawdown
gates.description: Max drawdown > -15% (i.e. drawdown shallower than 15%): the strategy must be survivable, not just profitable.

gates.name: regime_stability
gates.description: Worst-regime Sharpe > 0: the edge must not lose money in either the calm or the stress regime.

gates.name: beats_benchmark_net
gates.description: Annualized excess return vs benchmark, after the cost haircut, > 0: edge must beat buy-and-hold net of costs. Skipped (not failed) when no benchmark series is supplied.

gates.name: sortino
gates.description: Sortino >= 1.5: risk-adjusted return against downside volatility only. Sharpe punishes upside jumps; Sortino does not, so positively-skewed (trend-style) edges are judged on their pain, not their lottery tickets. For symmetric returns Sortino ~= sqrt(2) x Sharpe, so 1.5 is calibrated to the same elite bar as OOS Sharpe > 1.0. A secondary gate — DSR stays the primary statistical gate because the multiple-testing deflation math is built for Sharpe and has no clean Sortino analogue.

gates.name: calmar
gates.description: Calmar >= 2.0: annualized return at least twice the maximum drawdown (e.g. 20%/yr at a 10% maxDD). Return per unit of pain — complements the max-drawdown gate, which caps the pain but ignores how much return bought it. A secondary gate alongside Sortino.
